primary_question: When executable program wiring is part of the public candidate representation, can selective candidate routing reduce actual graph-execution work while preserving task capability?

primary_endpoint.name: selective_execution_work_fraction_at_capability
primary_endpoint.criterion: At each M, report the minimum exact graph-execution work fraction among registered budgets whose semantic success is at least 0.80 of exhaustive exact graph execution.

graph.description: Complete public executable program graph: node-local descriptors plus true program wiring.
graph.router_representation: frozen graph descriptor followed by learned candidate projection

summary.description: Public node-local structural summary with the graph-wiring field removed; matched candidate projection and query tower.
summary.router_representation: fixed public summary followed by learned candidate projection

execution_control.name: exact_graph_executor
execution_control.description: Deterministic topological execution using the candidate's public program wiring and Boolean operator semantics.
execution_control.purpose: establishes an executable-substrate ceiling independently of learned routing

leakage_rules: Router input contains public support input/output examples and public candidate graph descriptors.
Candidate program wiring is public in this experiment because executable graph structure is the registered intervention.
Target index, verifier-only examples, and outcome are evaluator-only.
Candidate pool construction does not condition decoy inclusion on router-visible support rows.
The twelve verifier-only rows are disjoint from the four router-visible rows and complete the 4-input truth table.
Primary evaluation targets are absent from router training in exact structure and complete truth table.

execution_work_contract.graph_edge_operations: one operation for each true program edge traversed during execution
execution_work_contract.structural_node_operations: one operation for each active non-input node executed

statistical_contract.primary_estimate: pooled trial-level semantic success and execution-work fraction
statistical_contract.primary_eligibility: exhaustive exact graph execution must have semantic success >= 0.80; a materially lower ceiling indicates an implementation error

promotion_rule: exact graph executor passes complete truth-table checks
train/evaluation structure and truth-table split checks pass
target identity is absent from router inputs
selective execution work is counted from actual graph operations
capability retention and execution work are both reported
no asymptotic scaling claim from finite M

persistent_experience.task_state: opaque address resolves router-visible task examples
persistent_experience.commit_rule: only a candidate that passes all verifier examples after exact graph execution may be committed
persistent_experience.intervening_writes: unrelated task records are inserted before anchor replay
persistent_experience.replay_metric: routing and adaptive execution work before versus after verified experience

decision_rule.condition: At M, a registered budget reaches at least 0.80 semantic retention versus exhaustive exact graph execution.
decision_rule.licenses: bounded evidence of capability-constrained selective execution under the registered executable-graph workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: asymptotic sublinear scaling, hardware speedup, general language capability, or universal program retrieval.

decision_rule.condition: No registered budget reaches 0.80 retention at M.
decision_rule.licenses: the registered router does not meet the capability-constrained criterion at that M.

freeze_rule.checkpointing: result files may be written after each seed/M without changing the scientific grid
